words.definition: used to say that you were unable to understand or solve something despite trying
words.example: I stared at the error message for an hour, but I couldn't figure it out.
words.exampleTranslation: 我盯著那則錯誤訊息看了一個小時，但還是搞不懂問題出在哪。
words.note: figure out 表示「搞懂、解決」，可接名詞或 wh- 子句，例如 figure out what went wrong

words.form: I will get back to you
words.definition: used to tell someone you will contact them again later with an answer or more information
words.example: Let me check with my manager, and I will get back to you by tomorrow.
words.exampleTranslation: 讓我跟主管確認一下，明天之前會再回覆你。
words.note: 常用於商務 email 或電話對話中，禮貌地表示現在無法立刻給答覆

words.definition: said right before something begins, often to show excitement, readiness, or mild resignation
words.example: Here we go—the presentation is about to start, so let's take our seats.
words.exampleTranslation: 開始囉，簡報要開始了，我們就座吧。
words.note: 語氣可正面（期待）也可帶點無奈，例如 Here we go again 表示「又來了」

words.definition: used to add another point to what was already said, often something additional or worse
words.example: The flight was delayed for three hours, and on top of that, they lost my luggage.
words.exampleTranslation: 班機誤點了三小時，除此之外，他們還弄丟了我的行李。
words.note: 常用來補充一個更多或更糟的狀況，語氣比 also 更強烈

words.definition: used to say that one's health, mood, or condition has clearly improved
words.example: I took some medicine and got some rest, and I feel much better now.
words.exampleTranslation: 我吃了藥又休息了一下，現在感覺好多了。
words.note: 可用於生理狀況（例如感冒後）或心理層面（心情好轉）

words.definition: used to introduce a result or conclusion that follows from what was just said
words.example: The store was closed, and so we decided to order dinner online instead.
words.exampleTranslation: 店關了，於是我們決定改成網路訂晚餐。
words.note: 語氣較口語隨性，正式寫作中較常用 therefore 或 as a result

words.definition: to prevent oneself or someone else from doing or expressing something; to restrain
words.example: She wanted to cry, but she held back her tears during the meeting.
words.exampleTranslation: 她很想哭，但在會議中忍住了眼淚。
words.note: hold someone back 指「阻礙某人」，hold back one's emotions 則指「克制自己的情緒」

words.definition: a fill-in-the-blank pattern used to describe someone's type or preference, such as "a morning person" (someone most alert early in the day) or "a dog person" (someone who loves dogs)
words.example: I'm definitely a morning person—I get most of my work done before noon.
words.exampleTranslation: 我絕對是那種早上型的人，我大部分的工作都在中午前完成。
words.note: 常見搭配：a people person（善於社交的人）、a cat person / a dog person（愛貓／愛狗的人）

words.definition: to acknowledge and appreciate minor achievements or progress, not just major successes
words.example: Even if the project isn't finished yet, let's celebrate the small wins along the way.
words.exampleTranslation: 即使專案還沒完成，我們也該慶祝一路上的小小成就。
words.note: win 在此作名詞，指「（小）成就、勝利」，常見於職場激勵語境

words.definition: used after a figurative or unusual expression to show that it's not meant literally
words.example: He's the glue that holds our team together, so to speak.
words.exampleTranslation: 可以這麼說，他就是把我們團隊凝聚在一起的黏著劑。
words.note: 通常放在句尾，用來緩和比喻性的說法，避免聽者誤以為是字面意思

words.definition: used informally to describe something as surprising, crazy, or hard to believe
words.example: It's wild how fast technology has changed in just the past ten years.
words.exampleTranslation: 光是過去十年科技變化的速度就快到太不可思議了。
words.note: 非常口語，常用於朋友間的閒聊，正式場合較少使用

words.definition: undecided or unable to choose between two options
words.example: I'm still on the fence about whether to accept the job offer.
words.exampleTranslation: 我還在猶豫要不要接受這份工作邀約。
words.note: 常搭配介系詞 about，例如 on the fence about something

words.definition: in addition to something, often something already significant or demanding
words.example: On top of her full-time job, she also takes care of her elderly parents.
words.exampleTranslation: 除了全職工作之外，她還要照顧年邁的父母。
words.note: 與 on top of that 是同一組片語的不同用法：on top of 後面接名詞，on top of that 則用來承接前一句

words.definition: to approach someone directly, usually in order to talk to them
words.translation: 走過來找我；主動跟我搭話
words.example: A stranger came up to me at the coffee shop and asked for directions.
words.exampleTranslation: 一個陌生人在咖啡店走過來跟我問路。
words.note: come up to + 人 強調主動靠近某人，常見於敘述初次相遇的情境

words.definition: an informal way of introducing what someone said, thought, or felt, often used in storytelling
words.example: He told me the trip was cancelled, and I was like, "Are you serious?"
words.exampleTranslation: 他告訴我旅行取消了，我當時就說：「你是認真的嗎？」
words.note: 非常口語的敘事用法，常見於年輕世代的對話，正式寫作應避免使用

words.definition: to spend time and effort trying to improve, complete, or fix something
words.example: I've been working on my presentation all weekend.
words.exampleTranslation: 我這整個週末都在忙我的簡報。
words.note: 後面可接名詞或動名詞，例如 work on improving your English

words.definition: an informal way of saying a large quantity or number of something
words.example: We got a whole bunch of feedback after launching the new app.
words.exampleTranslation: 我們推出新應用程式後收到了一大堆意見回饋。
words.note: 語氣輕鬆口語，意思接近 a lot of，但更強調數量之多

words.definition: a small, unspecified number of days, typically around two or a few
words.example: I'll need a couple of days to finish reviewing the contract.
words.exampleTranslation: 我需要幾天時間才能審閱完這份合約。
words.note: a couple of 字面是「兩個」，但口語中常泛指「幾個」，不一定剛好是兩個

words.definition: starting from the very beginning, without using any existing materials or preparation
words.example: The chef prefers to make every sauce from scratch instead of using store-bought ones.
words.exampleTranslation: 那位主廚偏好每一種醬料都從頭開始自製，而不是用市售的。
words.note: 常見搭配動詞 build / make / start + from scratch

words.definition: used to describe the sudden realization or understanding of something
words.translation: 我突然意識到；我突然想到
words.example: It hit me halfway through the meeting that I had forgotten to send the report.
words.exampleTranslation: 開會開到一半我才突然想起我忘了寄那份報告。
words.note: 常接 that 子句表示「突然意識到……」，近義說法還有 it dawned on me
